questions.text: In the source-audited joint taxonomy, what is the best description of a butt joint?

options.text: Two members meet end-to-face or edge-to-face and usually need a connector or fastener
Two members bypass each other through an overlap
The members are shaped into interlocking molded profiles
The joint is always waterproof without adhesive

questions.rationale: A butt joint is the simplest meeting of members and normally needs a mediating element such as a fastener or connector.
questions.explanation: Two 2.5 inch shear plates (roughly 3000—4000 lbf each) provide approximately 6000—8000 lbf total capacity, exceeding 4500 lbf. Wood-to-steel connections via shear plates are a standard design method. Philippine hardwoods (narra, molave, yakal) accept shear plates well; the issue is fastener corrosion, not wood compatibility. The Philippines' high humidity and salt air near coastal regions accelerate corrosion. Unprotected fasteners rust and lose strength; NSCP 2015 and AWPA standards mandate stainless steel (preferred) or ASTM A 153 Class D hot-dipped galvanized fasteners. Environmental context (tropical climate, humidity) drives material selection; failure to specify corrosion-resistant fasteners leads to premature loss of capacity.
questions.code_citation: NSCP 2015 Section 2401.7; AWPA U1 Standard (fastener material requirements)

questions.text: Which joint description matches an overlapping joint?

options.text: The members overlap or bypass each other so force can transfer through the overlap
Only the ends touch, with no overlap
The pieces are joined only by a surface coating
The joint is defined by mortar bedding

questions.rationale: An overlapping joint develops the connection by allowing one member to overlap or bypass another.
questions.explanation: This describes the tenon, not the mortise. This describes a dado joint. This describes a rabbet joint. A mortise is a precisely chiseled rectangular cavity (hole) into which the matching tenon (protrusion) is inserted. Mortise = cavity (receptacle); Tenon = protrusion. Always pair these terms correctly.
questions.code_citation: Timber Framers Guild Joinery Manual; NSCP 2015 Section 2401

questions.text: Which pairing follows the source-audited connector taxonomy?

options.text: Bolt - point connector; glue - surface connector
Glue - point connector; bolt - surface connector
Mortar - point connector; board foot - linear connector
Header - surface connector; stretcher - point connector

questions.rationale: The checked connection taxonomy identifies a bolt as a point connector and glue as a surface connector.
questions.explanation: 18% moisture is actually slightly high, not low; 12—15% is the target. Modern glues (PVA, polyurethane, epoxy) do require clamping pressure to achieve full strength and proper surface contact. Mortise-and-tenon joints are commonly glued; pins or wedges are used as supplementary security, not as replacements for glue. Optimal gluing conditions require wood moisture of 12—15% and clamping pressure of 100—200 psi. At 18% moisture, the wood is wetter than optimal; without clamping pressure, the glue cannot develop full strength and may not penetrate the joint surfaces uniformly, resulting in weak spots and potential early failure. Glue strength is a function of moisture content, clamping pressure, and curing time; neglecting any factor reduces joint capacity significantly.
questions.code_citation: NSCP 2015 Section 2401 (wood design); adhesive manufacturing specifications (PVA, epoxy, polyurethane)

questions.text: What is the key behavior of a pinned joint in the source-audited connection taxonomy?

options.text: It allows rotation at the joint
It prevents all rotation and all movement
It measures lumber volume
It creates a mortar bed

questions.rationale: A pinned joint allows rotation, unlike a rigid or fixed joint that maintains angular relationship.
questions.explanation: The connection has adequate initial capacity; the issue is durability and long-term strength loss. Galvanized coatings, while durable, are not indefinite; salt spray and humidity degrade them over decades. 3200 lbf is below the 3500 lbf rating; the connection is structurally adequate initially. While hot-dipped galvanized fasteners (ASTM A 153 Class D) provide excellent corrosion resistance, even galvanized coatings eventually corrode in high-humidity tropical environments with salt spray. Stainless steel (316 or 316L) offers superior long-term protection and maintains bearing strength longer. NSCP 2015 and AWPA standards recommend stainless for coastal and high-humidity locations. In tropical and coastal Philippine climates, specify stainless steel fasteners for connections that must maintain strength over 50+ years. Galvanized is adequate for interior and moderate-exposure applications.
questions.code_citation: NSCP 2015 Section 2401 (fastener materials); AWPA U1 Standard (fastener specifications for treated wood)

questions.text: What is the key behavior of a rigid or fixed joint?

options.text: It maintains the angular relationship between connected members
It always allows free rotation
It is used only for board-foot measurement
It is the same as a roller joint

questions.rationale: A rigid or fixed joint keeps the connected members from changing angle relative to each other.
questions.explanation: Both nails and bolts can rust; corrosion resistance depends on material, not form factor. Nails are used in Philippine hardwoods; the limitation is not material compatibility but load capacity. Threads contribute to bolt strength, but the primary load path in wood is bearing and friction, not thread-holding; nail strength is similarly fiber-based. Nails develop strength through friction against wood fibers and bearing at the nail shank. A single nail develops only 150—200 lbf in shear; multiple nails in staggered patterns are needed for higher loads. Bolts develop bearing strength across the full bearing area, which is larger, and transfer load through the bolt shank and threads together. Understand the mechanical basis of fastener strength: nails = friction + small bearing area; bolts = friction + larger bearing area + mechanical coupling.
questions.code_citation: NSCP 2015 Section 2301 (fastener capacity); AF&PA Design Values for Wood Construction

questions.text: Why is quartersawn lumber safer than plainsawn lumber where connection stability matters?

options.text: It has less shrinkage and distortion
It is always cheaper than plainsawn lumber
It eliminates the need for all fasteners
It converts cubic feet to cubic yards

questions.rationale: The wood source identifies quartersawn lumber as more dimensionally stable, with less shrinkage and distortion.
questions.explanation: Mortise-and-tenon joints are strong in tension but primarily resist racking; they do not have interlocking teeth. Lap joints overlap by reducing thickness but lack the interlocking geometry of dovetails. Butt joints rely entirely on fasteners and have no geometric lock. Dovetail joints feature interlocking tails and pins with angled geometry that creates a mechanical lock, distributing shear stress over large glue lines and resisting both lateral and withdrawal forces. Recognize dovetail geometry as the only joint type with interlocking tooth features that mechanically prevent both lateral and withdrawal motion.
questions.code_citation: NSCP 2015 Section 2401; Timber Framers Guild joinery standards

questions.text: Which connection-related advantage is associated with seasoned lumber?

options.text: More stable dimensions and better nail-holding than green lumber
Automatic waterproofing without treatment
Guaranteed termite immunity
A fixed board-foot price

questions.rationale: Seasoned lumber has reduced moisture-related movement and better nail-holding behavior than green lumber.

questions.text: Why is green lumber risky in a wood connection?

options.text: It can shrink or warp and weaken nail-holding as it dries
It is already kiln dried
It is measured only in cubic yards
It cannot contain sapwood

questions.rationale: Green lumber still contains excess moisture, so shrinkage, warping, and weaker nail-holding can affect the connection.

questions.text: Which statement is source-safe for plywood fastening near edges?

options.text: Plywood can receive nails or screws closer to the edge with less splitting than ordinary solid lumber
Plywood can never split at an edge
Plywood requires only mortar joints
Plywood edge fastening is a board-foot conversion

questions.rationale: George Salvan supports plywood taking nails or screws close to the edge with less splitting.
questions.explanation: Molave ('Queen of Philippine Woods') is denser and harder, better suited to heavy structural applications; its hardness makes fine joinery more difficult. Yakal is very stiff and strong but less decorative; reserved for heavy-duty structural use, not fine cabinetry. Tanguile is used in paneling and general carpentry, but narra is the traditional prestige choice for frames. Narra (Pterocarpus indicus) is the traditional choice for fine joinery and cabinetry in the Philippines. Its interlocked/wavy grain, medium to coarse texture, and good natural luster allow clean mortise-and-tenon joints. It glues and finishes well, making it ideal for visible frames. Match wood species to application: narra for fine joinery, molave for heavy structural work, yakal for high-stress environments.

questions.text: For a humid or wet exposure, which adhesive choice is safer than casein based on the checked material source?

options.text: Phenolic resin adhesive
Casein adhesive
Animal glue
No adhesive can be water-resistant

questions.rationale: The checked material source distinguishes adhesive families by water resistance. Phenolic resin is the safer water-resistant choice; casein is not safe for high-humidity or wet-dry exposure.
questions.explanation: While conservative practice may reduce this capacity by 25% for moisture or load duration, the nominal capacity exceeds 4000 lbf. Not all split rings exceed 6500 lbf; smaller rings (2.5 inch) develop only 2500—3200 lbf. 6200 lbf falls within the published 5000—6500 lbf range, so it does not exceed capacity by 200 lbf. Split ring capacity reference tables show a 4-inch diameter ring with 3/4 inch bolt develops 5000—6500 lbf, placing the 6200 lbf load within acceptable range (at the upper end). Know the relationship between ring diameter, bolt size, and capacity; do not confuse nominal capacity with allowable capacity under adjusted conditions.
